## b. Prepare the dataset for analysis

### Download gene annotation dataset
For comparable analysis, the same reference genome should be used for different datasets

```{r}
ah <- AnnotationHub()

# search for id of desired dataset

dbResult <- query(ah, c("EnsDb", "Mus musculus", "102")) 
dbResult[3]
str(dbResult)

# load mouse transcript dataset
MouseEnsDb <- ah[[dbResult$ah_id]]
str(MouseEnsDb)

# output data of interest in form of data.frame
annotations <- genes(MouseEnsDb, return.type = "data.frame")
```

### Load matadata and raw count, followed by clean up

Customisation required for this part, depending on how the data was labelled and where it was downloaded.


```{r}
## Load raw count matrix and metadata from Nextflow pipeline

raw_count_assay <- read_rds("sample_salmon.merged.gene_counts.rds")
raw_count_unfiltered <- assays(raw_count_assay)$counts    # raw count matrix

gse <- getGEO("GSE216252", getGPL = FALSE)
meta <- as.data.frame(gse[[1]])   # metadata

```

```{r}
## Filter for protein-coding genes (necessity of this step depends on the purpose of analysis)
raw_count <- raw_count_unfiltered |> rownames_to_column("gene_id") |> dplyr::filter(gene_id %in% annotations[annotations$gene_biotype == "protein_coding", ]$gene_id) |> column_to_rownames("gene_id")
```


```{r}
## Clean up metadata for later use

metadata <- meta |>   # Capture syntax to be changed according to the labels used while sampling
  dplyr::mutate(genotype = if_else(grepl("KO", title, fixed = TRUE), true = 'KO', false = 'C')) |> # genotype 
  dplyr::mutate(time = str_extract(meta$title, 'ZT(\\d*)', group = 1)) |> # time
  dplyr::mutate(replicate = str_extract(meta$title, 'rep (\\d*)', group = 1)) |> # replicate
  dplyr::mutate(experiment_accession = str_extract(meta$relation.1, 'term=(SRX\\d+)', group = 1)) |>
  # Note: SRX accessions are extracted to match the column names in the raw count file from QC
    dplyr::select(experiment_accession, genotype, time, replicate) |>
  rownames_to_column("geo_accession") |>
  arrange(geo_accession)

```



To this step, you should have the raw count and metadata dataframes in the following format:

```{r raw data check}
raw_count

metadata
```


## Exciting data analysis!!

Major steps were adapted from the workflow described in Bignon et al. 2023, with careful validation.

### Normalisation
#### 1. Convert to CPM & filter

```{r}
# Compute CPM
raw_count_cpm <- as.data.frame(raw_count) |>
  mutate(across(.cols = everything(), .fns = ~ . * 1000000 / sum(.), .names = "{col}"))

# Low count filter: at least CPM >= 1 in at least two samples
raw_count_cpm_filtered <- raw_count_cpm[rowSums(raw_count_cpm >= 1) >= 2, ]

```

Note: CPM values are not directly used in downstream analysis, it's only used to filter away genes with too low and insignificant abundance. TMM 

#### 2. TMM normalisation

```{r}
# Filter raw count based on cpm low count filter obtained in 1.
raw_count_filtered <- raw_count[rownames(raw_count) %in% rownames(raw_count_cpm_filtered),]

# Normalise library size of filtered raw count using TMM method
raw_count_filtered_norm <- DGEList(counts=raw_count_filtered) |> normLibSizes()
str(raw_count_filtered_norm)
raw_count_filtered_norm$samples

# log2 cpm with normalised library size
raw_filtered_norm_logcpm <- cpm(raw_count_filtered_norm, log=TRUE)
raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior <- cpm(raw_count_filtered_norm, log=TRUE, prior.count=3)

```



#### 1. Remove Unwanted Variance (RUV)

```{r}
# Check coefficient of variance: limma-trend (to be used) works best for similar library sizes across samples

cov <- sd(raw_count_filtered_norm$samples$lib.size) / mean(raw_count_filtered_norm$samples$lib.size) * 100
cov
```

5.3% is good!

```{r}
### RUV

x <- str_c(metadata$genotype,metadata$time,sep="_")
differences <- makeGroups(x)
controls <- rownames(raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior)

# k=2, prior (better to keep low but can increase if separation if quite poor in the PCA plots later)
RUVs_output_prior <- RUVs(raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior, controls, k=2, differences, isLog=TRUE)
raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior_RUVcount_k2 <- RUVs_output_prior$normalizedCounts
as.data.frame(raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior)
as.data.frame(raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior_RUVcount_k2)
W1 <- RUVs_output_prior$W[,1]
W2 <- RUVs_output_prior$W[,2]
```

### Diagnostic plots

### a. Variance plot across samples for unnormalised, TMM normalised and TMM & RUV normalised

```{r RLE-plots}

## filtered, unnormalised
plotRLE(as.matrix(raw_count_filtered), outline=FALSE, exprs_logged = FALSE,
        ylim=c(-0.9, 0.9), main = 'Unnormalised', xlab = "Samples", ylab = "Relative log", cex.main = 1.2)

## filtered, TMM normalised
plotRLE(raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior, outline=FALSE, exprs_logged = TRUE,
        ylim=c(-0.9, 0.9), main = 'TMM normalised', xlab = "Samples", ylab = "Relative log", cex.main = 1.2)

## filtered, TMM & RUV normalised
plotRLE(RUVs_output_prior$normalizedCounts, outline=FALSE, exprs_logged = TRUE,
        ylim=c(-0.9, 0.9), main = 'TMM & RUV normalised', xlab = "Samples", ylab = "Relative log", cex.main = 1.2)

```

#### b. PCA plots for unnormalised, TMM normalised and TMM & RUV normalised

```{r PCA-plots-1}
# PCA plot: CPM filtered raw count

pca_test_raw <- prcomp(t(raw_count_filtered), center=TRUE, scale=TRUE)
pca_df_raw <- as.data.frame(pca_test_raw$x)
pca_df_raw <- left_join(rownames_to_column(pca_df_raw, "experiment_accession"), metadata, by = "experiment_accession") |> dplyr::mutate(genotype = ifelse(genotype == "C", "WT", "Bmal1KO")) |> dplyr::mutate(genotype_fac = factor(genotype, levels = c("WT", "Bmal1KO")))
pca_df_raw$lightdark <- "light"
pca_df_raw$lightdark[pca_df_raw$time %in% c("0", "16", "20")] <- "dark"

ggplot(pca_df_raw, aes(PC1, PC2, color = interaction(lightdark, genotype_fac, sep=':'), label = time)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text(hjust=-0.2, vjust=-0.2, color = "black", size = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = 12, hjust = 0),
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_text(size=12),
    legend.text=element_text(size=10)
  ) + 
  labs(title = "",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(summary(pca_test_raw)$importance[2,1] * 100, 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(summary(pca_test_raw)$importance[2,2] * 100, 1), "%)"),
       color = 'Light condition:\nGenotype') 

```

### Rhythm analysis (JTK_cycle) and DE analysis (LimoRhyde)


### Annotation
```{r}
annotation_selection <- annotations |> 
    dplyr::select(gene_id, gene_name, description, entrezid) |>
    dplyr::filter(gene_id %in% rownames(raw_count_filtered))
```


### DE and rhythmicity detection

#### 1. Limorhyde

```{r}
period = 24
qvalRhyCutoff = 0.15

y = raw_filtered_norm_logcpm_prior # normalised but un-RUV-ed matrix is used

metadata_lmr <- metadata |>
  dplyr::select(experiment_accession, genotype, time) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(time = as.integer(time), cond = factor(genotype)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(title = meta$title) |> 
  dplyr::relocate(title, .after=experiment_accession)


metadata_lmr = cbind(metadata_lmr, limorhyde(metadata_lmr$time, 'time_'), W1, W2)
class(metadata_lmr)
setDT(metadata_lmr)
```

Note that the normalised but un-RUV-ed matrix should be used as *y* as RUV normalisation will be included using the two covariate matrices W1 and W2 later in *metadata_lmr*. This is to ensure that the data input is 'RUV-ed only once'.

```{r}
condNow <- "C"

design = model.matrix(~ time_cos + time_sin, data = metadata_lmr[cond == condNow])
fit = lmFit(y[, metadata_lmr$cond == condNow], design)
fit = eBayes(fit, trend = TRUE)
rhyNow = data.table(topTable(fit, coef = 2:3, number = Inf), keep.rownames = TRUE)
setnames(rhyNow, 'rn', 'gene_id')
rhyNow[, cond := condNow]

rhyLimmaSummary = rhyNow[, .(P.Value = min(P.Value)), by = gene_id]
rhyLimmaSummary[, adj.P.Val := p.adjust(P.Value, method = 'BH')]
setorderv(rhyLimmaSummary, 'adj.P.Val')
```

```{r}
# Relative log amplitude calculation

# Extract coefficients from your limma fit
coefs = coef(fit)[, c("(Intercept)", "time_cos", "time_sin")]

# Compute (log2 *relative*) amplitude for each gene
amplitude_lmr = sqrt(coefs[, "time_cos"]^2 + coefs[, "time_sin"]^2)
mean = coefs[, "(Intercept)"]

hist(amplitude_lmr, ylim = c(0,100))

rhyLimmaSummary <- rhyLimmaSummary |> left_join(rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(amplitude_lmr), "gene_id"))
lmr_rhythmic <- rhyLimmaSummary[rhyLimmaSummary$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & rhyLimmaSummary$amplitude_lmr > 0.29, ]$gene_id
lmr_rhythmic_unfiltered <- rhyLimmaSummary[rhyLimmaSummary$adj.P.Val < 0.05, ]$gene_id 
```

(Sinusoidal curves fitted to log2 data is asymmetric w.r.t. the baseline, hence relative log2 amplitude greater than 1 is possible.)

#### 2. JTK 

To classify genes as rhythmic or non-rhythmic in WT. Detailed guide of running JTK_CYCLE (v3) can be found here: https://openwetware.org/wiki/File:JTKversion3.zip.

MetaCycle could be explored for better accuracy. However, due to the regularity of the sampling time, JTK was deemed sufficient in my initial analysis.

```{r}
# Set upt the data input

JTK_matrix_RUV <- as.data.frame(RUVs_output_prior$normalizedCounts[,1:30])  # columns 1-30 are the WT data
JTK_matrix_RUV <- rownames_to_column(JTK_matrix_RUV, 'Probe')

# Create .txt files in the format used by JTK
write.table(JTK_matrix_RUV['Probe'], file = 'Sample_JTK/Bignon_sample_annot.txt', sep = '/t', row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE, quote=FALSE)
write.table(JTK_matrix_RUV, file = 'Sample_JTK/Bignon_sample_data.txt', sep = '\t', row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE, quote=FALSE)

```

--- Run JTK in _Bignon_sample_run.R_ ---
Ensure _JTK_CYCLE_v3_sample.R_, _Bignon_sample_annot.txt_ and _Bignon_sample_data.txt_ are in the right work directory.

Edit the script of _Bignon_sample_run_v3.R_ according to the sampling structure of the data, referencing the _JTK Users Guide (v3).doc_ and examples provided by the Hughes Lab. Note that missing samples can be accounted for in the analysis with appropriate setting.                                                                                                       

```{r JTK-wt}
JTK_output <- read.table(file = 'Sample_JTK/JTK.Bignon_JTK_run_v3.txt', header = TRUE ) |> dplyr::rename('gene_id' = 'Probe')

# Lable as rythmic & non-rhythmic using limorhyde's amplitude

JTK_output$amp_lmr <- amplitude_lmr[JTK_output$gene_id]
JTK_output <- dplyr::relocate(JTK_output, amp_lmr, .after = AMP)


JTK_output$Rhythmicity_lmrAMP <- 'Ambiguous'
JTK_output$Rhythmicity_lmrAMP[JTK_output$BH.Q > 0.1 | JTK_output$amp_lmr < 0.29] <- 'Non-rhythmic'
JTK_output$Rhythmicity_lmrAMP[JTK_output$BH.Q < 0.05 & JTK_output$amp_lmr > 0.29] <- 'Rhythmic'
JTK_output <- dplyr::relocate(JTK_output, Rhythmicity_lmrAMP, .before = BH.Q)
table(JTK_output$Rhythmicity_lmrAMP)
```



#### 3. Differential expression analysis with LimoRhyde

To compare expression levels between WT and mutant while accounting for rhythmicity. Detailed guide on how to run LimoRhyde can be found here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/limorhyde/vignettes/introduction.html.


```{r Limma}
design = model.matrix(~ cond + time_cos + time_sin + cond:time_cos + cond:time_sin + W1 + W2, data = metadata_lmr)

qr(design)$rank  # check if W1/2 are colinear with cond
cor(metadata_lmr[, c("W1", "W2", "time_cos", "time_sin")])  # check if W1/2 is eating away time information


fit = lmFit(y, design)
fit = eBayes(fit, trend = TRUE)
plotSA <- plotSA(fit)
deLimma = data.table(topTable(fit, coef = 2, number = Inf), keep.rownames = TRUE)
setnames(deLimma, 'rn', 'gene_id')

# record mean level of WT and KO!
mean_wt <- fit$coefficients[,1]
mean_ko <- fit$coefficients[,1] + fit$coefficients[,2]

# deLimma = deLimma[!(gene_id %in% drLimma[adj.P.Val <= qvalDrCutoff]$gene_id)] ## don't ignore differentially rhythmic genes
deLimma[, adj.P.Val := p.adjust(P.Value, method = 'BH')]
setorderv(deLimma, 'adj.P.Val')

deLimma

deLimma$diffExpressed <- 'NO'
deLimma$diffExpressed[deLimma$logFC>0.58 & deLimma$adj.P.Val<0.05] <- 'UP'
deLimma$diffExpressed[deLimma$logFC<(-0.58) & deLimma$adj.P.Val<0.05] <- 'DOWN'
table(deLimma$diffExpressed)

pdf("sample_diagrams//Bignon_plotSA.pdf", width = 5, height = 3.5)
plotSA(fit)
dev.off()
```

Proper variance-mean behaviour - DE analysis all good.

#### Effect of varying AMP and DE threshold (3D and 2D plots)

```{r}
### Create lists of thresholds
AMP_threshold_list <- seq(0, 2, by=0.05)
logFC_threshold_list <- seq(0, 5, by=0.1)


# Calculate the DE-rhythmic ratio at different threshold combinations
threshold_result <- data.frame(
  AMP = NA,
  logFC = NA,
  ratio = NA,
  rhythmic_DE = NA,
  DE = NA,
  rhythmic = NA,
  log_rhythmic_DE = NA
)

for (logFC_threshold in logFC_threshold_list){
  for (AMP_threshold in AMP_threshold_list){
    N_rhythmic_DE <- nrow(JTK_deLimma[abs(JTK_deLimma$logFC) > logFC_threshold & JTK_deLimma$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & JTK_deLimma$BH.Q < 0.05 & JTK_deLimma$amp_lmr > AMP_threshold])
    N_rhythmic <- nrow(JTK_deLimma[JTK_deLimma$BH.Q < 0.05 & JTK_deLimma$amp_lmr > AMP_threshold])
    # print(c(AMP_threshold, N_rhythmic))
    N_DE <- nrow(JTK_deLimma[abs(JTK_deLimma$logFC) > logFC_threshold & JTK_deLimma$adj.P.Val < 0.05])
    
    if (N_rhythmic == 0){
      DE_ratio = NA
    } 
    else{
      DE_ratio <- N_rhythmic_DE/N_rhythmic
    }
    threshold_result <- rbind(threshold_result, c(AMP = AMP_threshold, logFC = logFC_threshold, ratio = DE_ratio, rhythmic_DE = N_rhythmic_DE, DE = N_DE, rhythmic = N_rhythmic, log10_rhythmic_DE = log10(N_rhythmic_DE)))
  }
}

threshold_result <- drop_na(threshold_result)
threshold_result_finite <- threshold_result[is.finite(threshold_result$log_rhythmic_DE), ]

```

```{r GO}
## (Thanks Gemini for shortening this part of the code for me :>)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Background Gene Mapping (Run ONCE)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
bg_ids <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Mm.eg.db,
  keys = rownames(raw_count_filtered),
  columns = "ENTREZID",
  keytype = "ENSEMBL"
)$ENTREZID |> na.omit() |> unique()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Complete Processing Function (Export TSV + Plot with Title)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
process_gene_subset <- function(df, subset_name, bg_ids, plot_title, pval_cutoff = 0.05) {
  
  # A. Annotate & Save TSV File
  annot_df <- right_join(
    as.data.frame(annotations)[match(df$gene_id, annotations$gene_id), ],
    as.data.frame(df),
    by = "gene_id"
  ) |> arrange(desc(abs(logFC)))
  
  # Clean list columns if any exist to prevent write.table errors
  annot_df <- annot_df |> 
    mutate(across(where(is.list), ~ sapply(., paste, collapse = ";")))

  tsv_path <- paste0("Bignon_", subset_name, "_genes_annot.tsv")
  write.table(annot_df, file = tsv_path, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
  
  # B. Map Symbols to Entrez IDs
  sig_ids <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    org.Mm.eg.db,
    keys = df$gene_name,
    columns = "ENTREZID",
    keytype = "SYMBOL"
  )$ENTREZID |> na.omit() |> unique()
  
  # C. GO Enrichment
  ego <- enrichGO(
    gene          = sig_ids,
    universe      = bg_ids,
    OrgDb         = org.Mm.eg.db,
    keyType       = "ENTREZID",
    ont           = "BP",
    pAdjustMethod = "BH",
    pvalueCutoff  = pval_cutoff,
    qvalueCutoff  = pval_cutoff,
    readable      = TRUE
  )
  
  # Preview results in console
  print(head(as.data.frame(ego)))
  
  # D. Plotting with Title
  p <- dotplot(ego, showCategory = 10) +
    ggtitle(plot_title)
  
  pdf_path <- paste0("sample_diagrams/Bignon_GO_", subset_name, ".pdf")
  pdf(pdf_path, width = 6, height = 4)
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  
  print(p)
  
  return(list(annotated_df = annot_df, ego = ego))
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define Gene Subsets & Run All
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
gene_subsets <- list(
  "DE_rhythmic"     = JTK_deLimma[JTK_deLimma$BH.Q < 0.05 & JTK_deLimma$amp_lmr > 0.29 & abs(JTK_deLimma$logFC) > 0.58 & JTK_deLimma$adj.P.Val < 0.05, ],
  "DE_rhythmic_AMP" = JTK_deLimma[JTK_deLimma$BH.Q < 0.05 & JTK_deLimma$amp_lmr > 0.58 & abs(JTK_deLimma$logFC) > 0.58 & JTK_deLimma$adj.P.Val < 0.05, ],
  "DE"              = JTK_deLimma[abs(JTK_deLimma$logFC) > 0.58 & JTK_deLimma$adj.P.Val < 0.05, ],
  "rhythmic"        = JTK_deLimma[JTK_deLimma$BH.Q < 0.05 & JTK_deLimma$amp_lmr > 0.29, ]
)

# Custom plot titles for each section
titles <- c(
  "DE_rhythmic"     = "DE & Rhythmic Genes",
  "DE_rhythmic_AMP" = " & Rhythmic Genes (High AMP cutoff)",
  "DE"              = "DE Genes Only",
  "rhythmic"        = "Rhythmic Genes Only"
)

# Custom p-value cutoffs per subset (subset 1 uses 0.1, others 0.05)
pval_cutoffs <- c("DE_rhythmic" = 0.1, "DE_rhythmic_AMP" = 0.05, "DE" = 0.05, "rhythmic" = 0.05)

# Execute everything in one clean loop
results <- purrr::imap(gene_subsets, function(df, name) {
  process_gene_subset(
    df          = df,
    subset_name = name,
    bg_ids      = bg_ids,
    plot_title  = titles[[name]],
    pval_cutoff = pval_cutoffs[[name]]
  )
})
```
